name: observation
title: Observation
description: One claim heard or read in what came in to {{ identity.organisation.name }}: a call, an email, a document, a conversation. Each separate claim is its own entry, never one entry that summarises the passage: a paragraph of a call often holds five claims or more, so split it. Every entry is a decision, an action someone committed to, a question still open, a risk, a pain point, a requirement, a measure, an assumption or an outcome, and every one is traceable to words in the text, kept as its quote. Every figure, percentage, date and year the words state is kept exactly as stated. A passage that claims nothing, such as greetings or small talk, holds no entry.

files.observation.yaml:
unoverse: "1.0"
# ONE CLAIM HEARD OR READ in something that came in: a call, an email, a document, a
# conversation (docs/unoverse/data/objects/elements/observation.md, ruled 2026-10-07). Its own
# element, the one the platform adds beside EDGY's. It extends need, so it is written in the
# need's voice and lands beside the needs and tasks it bears on (owner, 2026-10-07: "it all
# lives in the same 3D space perfectly"). A pipeline writes it `per: section`, each one `of`
# the document it was read in, its section and pages on the line.
type: object
name: observation
element: observation
# THE GLYPH its rows are drawn with (README 4a): a lucide icon name.
icon: eye
extends: need
# THE SAME CLAIM IS ONE ROW: what kind it is and what it says.
uniqueBy: [kind, title]
# PLACED BY THE NEED'S SIX FIELDS, unchanged: the same voice is what puts it beside its tasks.
embed: [title, description, key_need, related_needs, questions, callToAction]
search: [universal_id, object_type, title, description, kind, quote, speaker, owner, due, true_as_of, app, source_url, source_id]
meta: open

# THE FACE, as a node's node.yaml carries it. The description is also the brief a section is
# read with, so it says what one observation is and how many a passage holds.
title: Observation
description: >-
  One claim heard or read in what came in to {{ identity.organisation.name }}: a call, an
  email, a document, a conversation. Each separate claim is its own entry, never one entry
  that summarises the passage: a paragraph of a call often holds five claims or more, so split
  it. Every entry is a decision, an action someone committed to, a question still open, a risk,
  a pain point, a requirement, a measure, an assumption or an outcome, and every one is
  traceable to words in the text, kept as its quote. Every figure, percentage, date and year
  the words state is kept exactly as stated. A passage that claims nothing, such as greetings or
  small talk, holds no entry.
whenToUse: >-
  What was said about this? What did we decide? Who committed to what, and by when? What is
  still open? What risks were raised?
category: Objects
version: 1.0.0

props: { $include: props }
files.props.yaml:
# AN OBSERVATION'S OWN FIELDS. Everything else it carries is the need's (objects/need/props.yaml).
# THE PROP IS THE BRIEF: each description is the whole instruction for its field.
#
# RE-BRIEFED from the need (README 5): the field and its limits are the need's, the brief is the
# observation's, so it is written in the need's voice and placed on the map by the same six
# fields.
title:
  description: >-
    The claim, as one plain statement with no person in it: 'Onboarding takes three weeks',
    'Move the launch to March', 'Send the data export by Friday'. Never 'I', 'we', 'you' or
    'they said'; who said it is the speaker field. Every figure and date exactly as stated.
description:
  description: >-
    The claim with what it is about, said plainly, with no person in it. Three sentences: what is
    claimed, what it concerns (the product, process, system or customer it is about), and why it
    matters or what follows from it, with every figure, date and condition the words state,
    exactly as stated. Never a word about the call or the document itself: never 'the speaker',
    'the call', 'the document states', 'was discussed'.
key_need:
  description: >-
    The need this claim bears on, in one line, with no person in it: 'Shorter onboarding for new
    customers', 'A launch date the team can hold'. It places the observation beside the needs and
    tasks it concerns.
related_needs:
  description: >-
    The smaller goals this claim touches, each a short verb phrase with no person in it, each
    naming its subject so it reads on its own: 'Confirm the launch date with marketing'. Only
    goals the claim itself bears on.
questions:
  description: >-
    The questions this claim raises or answers, each self-contained: it names its subject, so it
    reads without the passage around it. A question the claim answers is one a person would ask
    to find it.
audience:
  description: >-
    Who this claim concerns, in one or two words: customer, employee, partner, a named team or
    business unit. Read it from the passage.
callToAction:
  description: >-
    The next step this claim calls for, as one sentence: 'Confirm the March launch date with the
    marketing team'. For a question, what would answer it; for a risk, what would reduce it.
action:
  description: The next step as a label, one to three words, drawn from the call to action.

kind:
  type: string
  input: true
  enum: [decision, action, question, risk, pain-point, requirement, measure, assumption, outcome]
  description: >-
    What kind of claim this is. decision: something agreed. action: something a person
    committed to do. question: something open that needs an answer. risk: something that could
    go wrong. pain-point: something that hurts today. requirement: something that must be true.
    measure: a figure, with its unit and period. assumption: something taken as true without
    proof. outcome: a result that happened.
quote:
  type: string
  input: true
  description: >-
    The words in the text that make this claim, copied exactly as written, so it can be found
    there again. Only the words that say it, never the paragraph around them.
  maxLength: 600
speaker:
  type: string
  input: true
  description: >-
    Who made the claim, as the text names them: a speaker's name in a transcript, the sender of an
    email, the author of a document. Empty when the text does not say.
  maxLength: 80
owner:
  type: string
  input: true
  description: >-
    For an action or a question: who is to do it or answer it, as the text names them. Empty when
    the text names nobody.
  maxLength: 80
due:
  type: string
  input: true
  description: >-
    For an action: when it is due, as YYYY-MM-DD when the text gives a date, else the words it
    uses ('next week'). Empty when the text gives none.
  maxLength: 40
true_as_of:
  type: string
  input: true
  description: >-
    The date the claim speaks as of, as YYYY-MM-DD: the date the text states for it, else the
    date of the call, email or document it was made in. Empty when nothing gives one.
  maxLength: 10
